article_title: Wild-type p53 triggers a rapid senescence program in human tumor cells lacking functional p53.
study_model: EJ human bladder carcinoma cells lacking functional p53
intervention_or_exposure: Tetracycline withdrawal induced a wild-type p53 transgene. Re-addition switched expression off. EJ-CAT and p53-off cultures served as controls.
measurements: Colony formation after switching p53 off, BrdU incorporation and DNA-content flow cytometry, morphology, SA-β-gal staining, electron microscopy.
observed_outcome: p53 induction caused durable G1 and G2/M arrest, enlarged flattened cells, SA-β-gal staining and lipofuscin-like inclusions.
assessment: Supports rapid p53-induced senescence in EJ cells. The experiment did not test replicative exhaustion by serial passage.

study_model: Early-passage normal human diploid TIG-3 fibroblasts
intervention_or_exposure: Direct delivery of recombinant wild-type antennapedia–p16INK4A fusion protein. The study used buffer, p16 without the antennapedia tag and a functionally impaired antennapedia-tagged mutant as comparators across assays.
measurements: Tritiated thymidine incorporation, RB phosphorylation by immunoblot, morphology, SA-β-gal staining and persistence after washout.
observed_outcome: p16 delivery reduced DNA synthesis and RB phosphorylation, induced G1 arrest and increased SA-β-gal. Arrest and staining persisted seven days after washout.
assessment: Supports induction of features of replicative senescence by p16 delivery. The treated cultures were early passage. Late-passage senescent cells served as a comparator.
